title: Roger Taylor (Duran Duran drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: Roger Andrew Taylor, born 26 April 1960, Birmingham; raised in Shard End and Castle Bromwich. Began drumming at about twelve, teaching himself by playing along with records. Scent Organs (Melody Maker regional finals, 1978), briefly Cult Figures; joined Duran Duran in 1979. Influences named: Charlie Watts and Paul Thompson of Roxy Music. Played on Duran Duran, Rio, Seven and the Ragged Tiger, Arena and A View to a Kill; last show with the original line-up at Live Aid, Philadelphia, July 1985; left in 1986 ('the hermit of pop'). Percussion on the Power Station's Some Like It Hot; Arcadia's So Red the Rose; two tracks for Thank You (1994); rejoined 2001 (Astronaut, 2004, and the albums since); Rock and Roll Hall of Fame 2022.

title: Duran Duran - Wikipedia
notes: 'They hired Roger Taylor, a former member of various local bands.' 'After Live Aid and Arcadia, Roger Taylor left the band and retired to the English countryside, suffering from exhaustion.' The band 'hired Steve Ferrone to play drums while they searched for replacements' (1986); Sterling Campbell from late 1987, a member 1989-91. The 2001 reunion: 'John, Roger and Andy had rejoined.' Genres in the infobox: new wave, synth-pop, pop rock, dance-rock.

title: Update: Roger Taylor (Modern Drummer, Billy Amendola)
notes: December 2007, on Red Carpet Massacre. 'Tony Thompson was a very big influence on me. His playing on all those early Chic records and everything that Nile Rodgers produced was just great.' 'Another influence is John Bonham, of course.' Charlie Watts: 'He had this great organic snare sound.' 'I think some of the greatest drummers are not the most technical players in the world—like Ringo Starr.' 'I'm a big fan of dance music ... it all emanates from the beat ... it's all about the sound of the bass drum and the hi-hat.' 'John is quite a busy bass player who grew up on all these funky disco grooves.' 'I think you learn to be part of a song by playing with records. You learn to serve the song.' 'I used to be kind of tight in my playing ... I've loosened up a lot.' 'Give them space and room to breathe.' 'I like playing to a click.' 'We've used drum machines and programming in the past, and always mixed it with live instruments.' ''Hungry Like the Wolf' and 'Wild Boys' came from something Nick and I were doing together.' Gear then: a Tama acoustic kit, a Roland TD-20 V-Drum kit to his left, triggered samples; Zildjian, Pro-Mark, Aquarian. On the Power Station's Some Like It Hot: 'I got the Octobans out and did that part on the chorus—it's gated Octobans, basically.'

title: Duran Duran - A View To A Kill (MTV - Live Aid 7/13/1985)
notes: JFK Stadium, Philadelphia, 13 July 1985, MTV's broadcast. Taylor at about 1:55-2:10: a black sleeveless vest, short wavy dark hair, black gloves, headphones, blue trousers; a white Tama kit (TAMA on the bass drum's front head), chrome hardware, a rack of long black tube toms beside the hi-hat. Watched as contact sheets.

title: Planet Earth (Duran Duran song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded December 1980 at Red Bus, London, produced by Colin Thurston; Roger Taylor drums. Annie Zaleski: John Taylor's 'galloping bass' and Roger Taylor's 'stomping beats'; Rob Sheffield: Chic's bass line with the Sex Pistols' attitude.

title: Girls on Film - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded December 1980 at Red Bus, produced by Colin Thurston; released 13 July 1981. Annie Zaleski: 'the clicking camera sound before jumping into a funky rhythmic strut', 'Roger Taylor's percolating drums'.

title: Hungry Like the Wolf - Wikipedia
notes: Written and demoed in a Saturday at EMI's basement studio in spring 1982; re-recorded at AIR for Rio with Colin Thurston, keeping the demo's electronic backing track (a Roland TR-808 drum machine and a Jupiter-8), the bass and drums then added. Roger Taylor drums and percussion. US single labelled '130 B.P.M.'

title: Save a Prayer - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded January-February 1982 at AIR, London, produced by Colin Thurston, built round a sequencer track and an arpeggiated SH-2 riff; Roger Taylor drums. Album version 5:33.

title: Rio (Duran Duran song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded at AIR, Oxford Circus, produced by Colin Thurston; Roger Taylor drums and percussion; Andy Hamilton saxophone. Album version 5:33.

title: Is There Something I Should Know? - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded December 1982 at Good Earth, London, produced by Ian Little; mixes at several studios for 'a lack of compression on the drums'; for the final mix at RAK Alex Sadkin and Phil Thornalley 'replaced the drums with samples triggered via AMS delay units'. Roger Taylor drums. Single 4:11.

title: The Reflex - Wikipedia
notes: From Seven and the Ragged Tiger (1983), produced by Duran Duran, Alex Sadkin and Ian Little; 'heavily remixed by Nile Rodgers and Jason Corsaro for the single release' (1984). Album version 5:29, single 4:25.

title: A View to a Kill (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded early 1985 at Maison Rouge and CTS, London, with a sixty-piece orchestra; produced by Bernard Edwards, Jason Corsaro and Duran Duran, John Barry arranging and conducting. Roger Taylor drums. Released 6 May 1985, 3:37.

title: Notorious (Duran Duran album) - Wikipedia
notes: 'By the time it came to record the new album at the beginning of 1986, drummer Roger Taylor had quit the group, citing exhaustion.' Steve Ferrone, session drummer, 'drums on all tracks', with Nile Rodgers producing.
